- Overestimate prices when sentiment is high (especially >0.5) and recent history shows upward momentum.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is low (especially <0.3) or shows negative drift, especially after recent spikes.
- Avoid over-optimistic forecasts after sharp price spikes; reduce forecasted overshoot by 10–15% in the immediate aftermath.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment strongly supports continuation.
- Lagged sentiment effect: if sentiment drops below 0.3 for 3+ consecutive days, reduce forecasted trend by 5–10% to account for weakening momentum.
- Horizon-specific: for 30-day forecasts, avoid assuming continuation of recent trend if sentiment is mixed or declining; favor smoother, lower volatility paths.
